notes.title: Community Update: A New Direction
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone,[/p][p]Thank you again for all your valuable feedback on the Norah's Song demo. Your insights have been incredibly helpful, and I truly appreciate the time and thought you put into trying it out.[/p][p]After much consideration and deeply reviewing the comprehensive feedback, I've decided to [b]shift to a completely new game idea[/b]. The demo served its purpose perfectly by highlighting the need to revisit some fundamental choices. Ultimately, as I looked at the final shape of Norah's Song and its storyline, I realized it wasn't aligning with the vision I had for a truly impactful experience, and frankly, I don't feel it's good enough for release.[/p][p]This wasn't an easy decision, but the feedback you provided helped me see that an alternative concept carries more depth and offers greater potential for development. Rest assured, all the valuable input you shared will be carried forward and applied to this new project. My priority remains to build an even stronger, more polished experience that truly resonates with players.[/p][p]This is all still a work in progress, and I'm excited about what's next. Thank you again for your detailed feedback.[/p]

notes.title: Development Update
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone,[/p][p]Thank you again for all your valuable feedback on the [b]Norah's Song[/b] demo. Your insights have been incredibly helpful.[/p][p]I've decided to [b]deactivate the demo[/b] for now. The comprehensive feedback highlighted the need to revisit some fundamental choices made during the game's development, which was exactly why I released the demo instead of developing blindly without community input. My priority is to ensure [b]Norah's Song[/b] aligns as closely as possible with player interests and preferences while still retaining its unique identity. This step will help us build an even stronger, more polished experience for you.[/p][p]This is all still a work in progress. Thank you again for your detailed feedback and for trying the demo![/p]

notes.title: Demo Patch
notes.notes:
[p][b]Hey everyone,[/b][/p][p]Thanks again for all the feedback on the [b]Norah’s Song[/b] demo. I’ve just pushed an update that includes:[/p][list][*][p]Fix for the clipping issue after the move to UE 5.6. It still happens in some edge cases with motion matching, which I’ll refine in a future update[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced head movement. A customization option for this and FOV is planned[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the camera blur issue when toggling the flashlight or getting too close to walls[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the camera going out of focus unexpectedly[/p][/*][/list][p]To respond directly to a detailed comment that caught my attention:[/p][p]Yes, the camera clipping is a real issue, especially around tight spaces like windows and lamps. I’m working on better collision handling to stop that from happening. The floaty camera and exaggerated wobble were toned down in this update, and more options are coming to let you adjust that to your preference.[/p][p]The flashlight blur and strange focus behavior were caused by an unintended post-processing effect. That’s been fixed. As for the doors, you’re right. They lacked proper feedback, and input was getting stacked. I’ve started reworking the interaction system to feel more responsive and grounded.[/p][p]This is all still a work in progress. I appreciate everyone’s patience and honesty. Every comment helps.[/p][p][b]More updates soon.

Thank you [url="https://steamcommunity.com/id/copogu4"][u]copogu4[/u][/url][u], [/u][/b][dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/id/sonoket"][/dynamiclink], [dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/id/anothernewhuman"][/dynamiclink], [dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/id/caro12345/"][/dynamiclink] for your feedback and trying the demo![/p]

notes.title: Steam Next Fest Demo Released & What's Next
notes.notes:
[p]Hey everyone,
I'm really excited (and a little nervous) to share the [b]demo for Norah’s Song[/b], my first ever game project.[/p][p]As a solo developer just starting out, I’ve built this using a mix of purchased assets and my own work while learning along the way. I know it’s not perfect, and there’s still a lot to improve, but this is an important first step, and I’m proud to have made it this far.[/p][p]This demo is just the beginning. I’ll be listening closely to feedback and updating it over time. The final game will include a much deeper story and a more polished experience shaped by everything I learn from this phase.[/p][p]Thanks so much for checking it out and supporting this journey.
More updates, improvements, and content are definitely on the way.[/p]

notes.title: Norah's Song is Coming to Steam Fest!
notes.notes:
I'm super excited to share that Norah's Song will be part of the upcoming Steam Fest.

This means you'll get to play a special demo I've put together just for the festival. It's your first chance to experience a descent into a fragmented psyche, navigating a haunting world shaped by memory, trauma, and loss. You'll get a taste of the reality-bending shifts, the tense moments of hiding and evasion, and the atmospheric world I'm building.

To give you a little sneak peek before then, I'm also uploading a new teaser trailer today – keep an eye out for it!

Get ready to explore a mind fracturing under pressure, where love and loss intertwine.

If this sounds like your kind of journey, please consider Wishlisting Norah's Song on Steam! It helps me out a ton as a solo dev and keeps you in the loop.

I honestly can't wait for you to try it out. Hope to see you (virtually) at Steam Fest!
